sheets.name: A_天气屋与周边全景_三版黑白小稿
sheets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: early ENVIRONMENT VALUE-THUMBNAIL composition exploration for the cozy fairy-tale game "Weather House".
Deliverable: ONE portrait contact sheet containing EXACTLY THREE wide landscape thumbnails stacked vertically, separated by white gutters. Each thumbnail has a landscape 16:9 composition; the whole board is roughly 3:5 portrait. Small plain black panel IDs in the white margin only. No titles, captions or other text.
Primary purpose: show three genuinely different compositions of ONE location so the designer can choose a layout before color. Change viewpoint, framing, horizon, balance of large shapes and light-dark arrangement. Start fresh with designed forms, not a recolored or filtered detailed illustration.
Visual language: very rough professional 2D concept massing sketches, only FOUR or FIVE neutral grayscale value groups. Broad confident opaque brush silhouettes, loose slightly irregular edges and occasional lost edges, very sparse descriptive strokes. Large flat untextured areas are essential. Simplify foreground / midground / background into connected masses. Light areas deliberately guide the eye; keep a coherent walkable ground plane. Friendly crooked asymmetrical tree and building silhouettes, shape design rather than generic perfectly round stock trees. Each thumbnail must read at postage-stamp size. 20–40 major shapes per panel, no fine rendering. Tiny chibi witch with floppy hat, short cape and wooden wand may appear only as a simple scale silhouette. All animals are simple rounded natural animal silhouettes.
Weather direction MUST be respected: NEVER include a small self-contained floating cloud hovering above a prop, animal or moss patch. If rain is shown, a continuous natural overcast sky above the treetops produces rainfall across a broad stretch of landscape and depth; imply it with a few sparse strokes, reduced distant contrast, and simple puddle masses. Clouds are large-scale weather and may extend beyond the picture boundaries. Do not depict rain as a single narrow column or a weather icon.
Avoid: any color or sepia; photorealism; 3D rendering; realistic shading; gradients everywhere; texture noise; individual leaves, grass blades, bark, flower petals, roof tiles, costumes or facial detail; elaborate effects; pencil outlines and crosshatching; polished finished illustrations. No cinematic epic scale, giant fantasy monuments, castle or city. No tiny floating rain cloud. No watermark. Keep everything visually simpler than a finished painting.
Location A: the weather witch's home at the edge of a small forest. A squat single-storey cottage with a broad slightly crooked moss roof, round window and tiny porch; one old companion tree; clear entry path; a nearby pond and gentle distant hill may be suggested very economically. Cottage is the primary focal point. Keep one coherent design family for the house in all three options. Daylight is expressed only through flat value shapes.
A1, top: sheltered arrival. Eye-level view from a dark forest threshold. Tree trunks crop both sides and a diagonal branch frames the top. A light winding path leads from lower left into a lit clearing, cottage on right third. Foreground dark connected mass, middle light opening, pale quiet distance. The tree beside the cottage has a leaning forked silhouette.
A2, middle: open hill shoulder. Cottage on left third in side three-quarter view; old tree leans behind it. A single broad diagonal grassy hill plane crosses the foreground; path comes from the right. Low horizon and large quiet sky occupy nearly half the frame. Small pond is only one pale distant shape. Broadest, airiest composition.
A3, bottom: across a small pond, closer than a panoramic landscape. Large pale water shape fills foreground bottom half and leads to a short stepping-stone route at the left edge; cottage and irregular tree cluster occupy middle right with a strong asymmetric roof silhouette. Dark reeds crop one corner; one or two flat reflection marks. Strong horizontal balance with the tree providing vertical accent.
Labels exactly A1, A2, A3. These are composition alternatives, not a sequence.

Location B: the FIRST animal-request courtyard, not a human village. The rack and moss bed are close enough to belong to one small courtyard. No human house as main subject; at most a tiny distant roof hint.
All THREE B options depict the same gentle broad rainy weather BEFORE the weather is repaired. Rain belongs to the whole clearing: sparse strokes across the full width and depth, a single broad pale overcast opening above canopy, simple wet ground shapes. The tree canopy can shelter some of the ground naturally. No sunny spotlight on the rack, no hovering cloud, no narrow column of rain. B1, top: low eye-level courtyard framed by a giant crooked tree trunk on left; hollow midway up, rack at its foot left-center, moss bed right-center. A broad light path/clearing shape connects the two requests in the middle. The witch is a tiny lower-center silhouette; tree and shrubs combine into one dark upper frame. Show the entire activity space.
B2, middle: moderate elevated three-quarter view revealing the layout. A forked trunk occupies top center, rack left, moss bed right, irregular pale wet ground in between; the tiny witch enters along a curved route from lower right. Foreground branches crop only one corner. Clearly organized spatial diagram within an actual perspective scene, not top-down plan or isometric asset sheet.
B3, bottom: intimate view past the drying rack in the near-left foreground. The rack and one hanging broad leaf are large simple dark framing silhouettes. A diagonal path goes toward the frog's moss bed at middle-right, old tree hollow sits behind at upper-left. Pale rainlit gap between tree trunks beyond. Strong near-large / far-small relationship, with uninterrupted traversable ground between animal stations.
Labels exactly B1, B2, B3.

A rounded bird can perch on a branch, a tiny deer may stand on the opposite bank; they are optional tiny scale accents. Water should be one designed value shape with 2–3 ripple/reflection strokes maximum. Trees and grassy banks remain very simple. Quiet diffuse daytime with no conspicuous cloud object. One coherent pond design family, different compositions.
C1, top: eye-level approach along the bank. Dark reeds and leaning trunk frame left; bright crescent pond curves from lower right toward center; a large canopy occupies upper right. Small witch on a light middle bank and tiny deer across the water. A clearly readable S-curve through shore and water, broad calm surface.
C2, middle: low near-water viewpoint. Very large quiet pale horizontal water shape fills the lower half; far bank is a dark connected strip with irregular tree forms. The witch sits or crouches at the left third, a simple branch with bird crops the near right edge. A single arching tree limb frames upper portion; balance intimate large foreground branch against small distant character. Strong horizontal composition.
C3, bottom: higher overlook from a rocky path. The pond appears as an asymmetric oval light shape in a dark wooded bowl, with a narrow opening to a pale background at upper left. A small natural log/stepping stones breaks one edge without dominating. Witch silhouette near a diagonal lower-left rock shelf leads the eye into the water. Layered depth but a modest small pond, not a canyon. Strong oval focal shape and diagonal foreground.
Labels exactly C1, C2, C3.
